title: OpenAI raised another $11B - implied $1.25T book valuation
gist: A forum post quoting Reuters says OpenAI closed an initial $11 billion of a round valuing it at $1.25 trillion, well short of its up-to-$30 billion target and below the $1.5 trillion it first sought. The article adds that AI sentiment has cooled, with Anthropic's planned IPO valued at about $1.5 trillion versus earlier expectations of roughly $2 trillion.

insights.claim: OpenAI closed $11 billion of new funding, the initial part of a round valuing the company at $1.25 trillion, according to a source quoted by Reuters.
insights.speaker: Xebec
insights.so_what: Sets a mark for private AI valuations that is the basis for read-through to the AI capex complex.
insights.quote: OpenAI has closed ‌on new funding of $11 billion

insights.claim: The $11 billion raised so far is only a portion of OpenAI's original target of up to $30 billion, and the valuation has come down from the $1.5 trillion level it initially sought, per two investors.
insights.speaker: Xebec
insights.so_what: A smaller raise at a lower valuation signals investor price resistance to AI mega-rounds.

insights.claim: SoftBank and MGX participated in the OpenAI funding, according to the investors.
insights.speaker: Xebec
insights.so_what: Capital continues to come from a few large strategic and sovereign-linked backers.

insights.claim: Sentiment toward AI companies has cooled in the last month, with some investors valuing Anthropic's planned IPO at about $1.5 trillion, below earlier expectations of roughly $2 trillion.
insights.speaker: Xebec
insights.so_what: Lower IPO valuation expectations point to a sentiment peak risk for AI-linked equities and suppliers.
insights.quote: Sentiment toward AI companies has cooled in the last month

insights.claim: Taken together, the OpenAI raise coming in below its target size and initial valuation and the lower Anthropic IPO marks suggest AI private-market valuations are compressing from earlier highs.
insights.speaker: Xebec
insights.so_what: Inference from the reported figures; relevant to AI-capex funding conditions.
